## My Reasoning

I've been farming this land in Quzhou for over 40 years. I know the North China Plain. The soil here is deep loam, the water table is reachable, and the growing season gives me exactly two slots per year. There is no question in my mind what I will plant: winter wheat followed by summer maize. That is what this land is for. That rotation has fed my family, that rotation is what the county grain procurement system supports, and at 65 I am not going to gamble on cotton or vegetables — my back cannot take it and the market risk is not worth it on 10 mu.

**Winter wheat** goes in October. I will use Jimai 22 — I have used it for six years now and it gives me consistent 500 kg/mu on my plots. I rotary-till after the maize harvest to work in the stalks. I apply compound fertilizer as the base before sowing and top-dress with urea at jointing in March. Four irrigations: pre-sowing moisture irrigation, the winter irrigation before the ground freezes, jointing water, and heading water. I know farmers who skip the winter irrigation to save money on electricity — I do not. Skipping it costs yield. I spray herbicide in winter and do one fungicide-insecticide pass around heading for powdery mildew and aphids. That is enough.

**Summer maize** goes in directly after the June wheat harvest, the same 10 mu. No ploughing — straight seeding into the wheat stubble. I use Zhengdan 958; the county extension station keeps pushing newer hybrids but Zhengdan 958 is reliable and I know how it behaves. Summer rainfall in Quzhou usually covers the bulk of what maize needs, but I will irrigate once at silking if the forecast looks dry — that stage is critical and I will not let it miss water. One herbicide pass after emergence, one more treatment if corn borer pressure shows up in late July. I expect around 580 kg/mu.

My education tells me to test the soil and calibrate fertilizer. My experience tells me roughly what my fields need after 40 years of growing the same crops here. My nitrogen rates are moderate — I've watched neighbors burn money putting down 30+ kg/mu with no yield gain over my 18–20.
